subject: Provisional latency derating & provisional credit proposal during FinSec migration
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@finsec-analytics.com>, contracts@finsec-analytics.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Provisional latency derating & provisional credit proposal during FinSec migration

Alex / FinSec contracts team —

Quick note to outline a remediation path we propose ahead of your scheduled data-migration (June 14-16) that may temporarily raise observed p95s for hosted inference. We want to avoid surprises and lock in an operational fallback that protects your production SLAs while the migration completes.

Proposal (short):
- Temporary SLO derating window: 72 hours starting at migration kickoff (June 14 02:00 UTC).
  - During the window we will measure p50/p95 over a 15-minute sliding window rather than the standard 1-hour aggregation to avoid penalizing transient warmups.
- Provisional credit: If p95 exceeds the contracted threshold for more than two 15-minute windows in the 72h, we will issue a prorated service credit capped at 5% of monthly invoice for the affected days. (Calc attached.)
- Evidence & telemetry: Redwood will deliver an evidence package within 48 hours of the window close — token-level latency histograms, routing logs, prefix cache hit rates, and example traces showing KV cache warmup artifacts.
- Monitoring/playbook: Monica (CC) will run a daily checkpoint during migration and coordinate any immediate mitigations (routing to dedicated pool / temporary autoscale).

Why this approach? During mass-key churn (re-index / migration) KV cache warmups + initial cold L3 cache fills can create short-lived p95 spikes that do not reflect steady-state experience. A short, sample-focused measurement and a pre-agreed credit avoids long disputes while we validate fixes.

Attachments: SLO_Evidence_Plan_20270607.pdf, ProvisionalCredit_Calc_sheet.xlsx

Ask: Please confirm acceptance of this temporary derating + credit approach or propose alternate wording you need in the contract addendum. If contracts approve, we request delegated sign-off to implement the monitoring/playbook (see Monica) so we can run pre-migration canaries.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@finsec-analytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@finsec-analytics.com
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 10:05:18 -0700
Subject: Re: Provisional latency derating & provisional credit proposal during FinSec migration

Ben — thanks for the quick summary. A couple of clarifying questions before we loop procurement in: 

1) Can you formalize the exact p50/p95 thresholds that will be considered "exceeding"? Our current contract references p50 <= 120ms and p95 <= 650ms. Is the provisional credit triggered only if p95 > 650ms?
2) The 15-minute sliding window is fine but we need a guarantee on the sampling frequency and that you won't backfill noisy samples to inflate counts. What sampling/aggregation method will you use?
3) On evidence: will the evidence package include request IDs so we can cross-check server-side traces in our observability?

Also cc'ing our contracts mailbox — please advise if a short contract addendum (1 paragraph) is sufficient or if you need a formal amendment.

On Tue, Jun 8, 2027 at 10:05 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex / FinSec contracts team —
> 
> Quick note to outline a remediation path we propose ahead of your scheduled data-migration (June 14-16) that may temporarily raise observed p95s for hosted inference. We want to avoid surprises and lock in an operational fallback that protects your production SLAs while the migration completes.

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@finsec-analytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@finsec-analytics.com
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 14:47:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Provisional latency derating & provisional credit proposal during FinSec migration

Alex — happy to take this one on operationally. A few specifics to answer your questions and to make the evidence package actionable: 

- Thresholds: yes — provisional trigger will be p95 > 650ms (matches contract). We will also report p50 distributions for context but the credit triggers off p95 only.
- Sampling & aggregation: we will compute true per-request latency at ingress, no downsampling. For SLO evaluation during the 72h derate window we will use contiguous 15-minute bins and count a bin as "breached" if p95 of that bin > 650ms. The breach condition requires >2 breached bins in the 72-hour window to qualify for credit. We will not retroactively add historical samples — only live ingestion timestamps are used.
- Evidence ids: each request row in the evidence CSV will include a request_id, model_version, route_id, region, kernel_variant, backend_node_id, and a trace_link to the corresponding trace in your observability (when available).
- Mitigations we can run during the window: (a) redirect a percentage of traffic to your Dedicated pool for latency-sensitive routes; (b) temporary burst autoscale increase for the affected region; (c) enable prefix-level cache pre-warm for known keys. We'll operate under your direction.

I'll attach the SLO_Evidence_Plan and a sample evidence CSV template in the follow-up (see file: SLO_Evidence_Plan_20270607.pdf). If contracts prefer, we can draft a 1-paragraph addendum and submit it for e-signature. Ben — can you confirm whether legal wants a specific phrasing for the credit cap or if the spreadsheet is sufficient?

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@finsec-analytics.com>, contracts@finsec-analytics.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Provisional latency derating & provisional credit proposal during FinSec migration

Alex / Contracts team / Karthik —

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Alex. Monica's text looks good and matches what I verbally proposed. A couple follow-ups and a request for delegated approval: 

- Confirmed triggers: p95 > 650ms per 15-minute bin, >2 bins in 72h for credit.
- Credit calculation: prorated by affected hours in the month, capped at 5% — sheet attached.
- Evidence contents: Monica called out the columns — we'll include request_id + trace link.
- Delegation ask: Karthik, can you approve a one-paragraph contract addendum for this one (language to be drafted below) so contracts can e-sign before migration? If you approve, we'll push the addendum to DocuSign and run our pre-migration canaries on June 12.

Draft addendum language (for quick edit):
"During the scheduled data migration window (June 14-16, 2027), Redwood Inference and FinSec Analytics agree to a provisional SLO measurement adjustment as follows: SLO evaluation for the duration of the migration will use contiguous 15-minute aggregation bins; a provisional credit will be issued if p95 latency exceeds 650ms for more than two such bins within the 72-hour window. Credits will be prorated for affected hours and capped at 5% of the monthly invoice. Redwood will provide an evidence package within 48 hours after the window close. This provision is temporary and limited to the migration event described above."

If Karthik approves, I will move DocuSign and coordinate the canary run with Monica. Alex — once contracts give an OK we will also add a dedicated monitoring dashboard and a one-click routing knob to shift 10% of traffic to Dedicated pool if needed.

Ben
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
